transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I messed up at work. I pushed ahead with this big onboarding launch and committed company money, plus vendor time, before any of the approvals were actually in place. At the time, it just felt bold and necessary, like I was getting things done. But now... now I'm on administrative leave, and everyone is asking me what I was thinking. So, my job sent me here.
During that period leading up to the launch, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual?
No, not really. I mean, I was sleeping about the same as I always do. I didn't notice any change with that.

Yeah, I suppose I did. For the past few weeks, I felt... just brilliantly alive, honestly. Like I could finally show leadership what HR can really be. But then, on the flip side, I would get suddenly furious if someone questioned me. Even over really small things, like minor edits or just routine budget questions. So it was either feeling amazing and capable, or getting incredibly angry at anyone who I felt was slowing me down.
Have you ever experienced a period in your life lasting at least two weeks where you felt deeply down, depressed, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I get stressed out by work or have a bad day sometimes, just like anyone else, but... no, I've never had a stretch of two weeks where I felt deeply down or just stopped caring about things. That hasn't really been an issue for me.
During that time, did your thoughts feel like they were racing or moving much faster than usual?
No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... my mind was definitely focused on the project, but my thoughts didn't feel like they were racing or out of control. They were just moving at a normal pace, really.
